note: Adapted from Harris (1966). Originally described by Silvestri (1912) as a subspecies of A. crucifer and raised to species rank by Grassé; Harris (1966) did not redescribe the morphology and gave only measurements of specimens from Ghana and Nigeria together with diagnostic characters, so this entry is mainly measurements and diagnosis. Units millimetres; major soldier n=10, minor soldier n=5.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: Originally a subspecies of A. crucifer (Silvestri 1912), later raised to species rank by Grassé. According to Silvestri it differs from A. crucifer in the shorter mandibles of the major soldier; according to Grassé the head of the major soldier is more rectangular and the mandibular apex more strongly curved. In the key it is separated from A. crucifer by the following combination — "sides of the head compressed, narrowed anteriorly, slightly flattened posteriorly, mandibles straight and incurved at the apex, right mandible without a basal tooth" — whereas A. crucifer has an oval head, stout mandibles each with a median marginal tooth, and a reduced basal tooth on the right mandible.

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: Measurements (mm; table of the original, specimens from Ghana and Nigeria, the mean in parentheses): head length including mandibles, major soldier 1.82—2.09 (1.93), minor soldier 1.50—1.54 (1.52); head length 1.18—1.36 (1.26), 0.91; head width 1.14—1.23 (1.15), 0.82—0.86 (0.84); left mandible length 0.68—0.82 (0.77), 0.68—0.77 (0.73); pronotum width 0.82—0.91 (0.87), 0.64—0.68 (0.67); hind tibia length 1.00—1.14 (1.04), 0.86—0.91 (0.90). The original notes that these specimens are slightly smaller than the values recorded for Portuguese Guinea and the Ivory Coast (head width 1.26 mm).
